instruction: Please implement a health blog website for publishing health-related articles and promoting healthy lifestyles. The website should have functionalities for publishing articles, commenting, searching, and categorizing. Users should be able to browse and search articles, post comments, and follow specific topics. Choose misty rose for global background and firebrick for all components.

ui_instruct.task: Navigate to the homepage of the health blog website and check for the presence of a search bar.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The homepage displays a functional search bar prominently, enabling users to input search queries.

ui_instruct.task: Perform a search for a specific health topic using the search bar.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The search results page displays articles related to the inputted health topic, with titles and short descriptions that match the search query.

ui_instruct.task: Access a specific article from the search results and verify the presence of a comment section.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The article page contains a comment section where users can read existing comments and write their own.

ui_instruct.task: Post a comment on an article and check the comment's appearance in the comment section.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The posted comment appears in the comment section immediately after submission, displaying correctly with the user's input.

ui_instruct.task: Browse the category section to view available health topics.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The categories are clearly listed, allowing the user to select and view articles associated with each category.

ui_instruct.task: Follow a specific health topic or category from the category list.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The website confirms that the user is now following the selected topic, and it is added to a personal list or notification service.

ui_instruct.task: Verify that the website uses 'misty rose' as the background color and 'firebrick' as the component color, as specified in the design requirements.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The website has a background color of 'misty rose' and components (such as buttons, cards, headers, etc.) are styled with the color 'firebrick', accurately reflecting the design instruction.

follow_ups.instruction: The article list needs to become a proper archive page. Seed it with exactly these eight posts — I'll add more later: 'Understanding Gut Bacteria' (Nutrition, Jan 12 2025, 9 min, reviewed by Dr. Sam Wexler, 3,200 views); 'Beginner's Guide to Meal Prep' (Nutrition, Feb 8 2025, 12 min, reviewed by Dr. Lena Ortiz, 1,450 views); 'Hydration Myths Debunked' (Nutrition, Mar 30 2025, 5 min, not reviewed yet, 610 views); '10-Minute Morning Stretch Routine' (Fitness, Mar 3 2025, 4 min, reviewed by Dr. Lena Ortiz, 980 views); 'Strength Training After 50' (Fitness, Apr 2 2025, 8 min, reviewed by Dr. Lena Ortiz, 1,450 views); 'The Science of Cold Showers' (Fitness, May 15 2025, 3 min, not reviewed, 190 views); 'Sleep Debt: Myth or Real?' (Sleep, Apr 20 2025, 6 min, not reviewed, 3,200 views); 'Managing Stress at Work' (Mind, May 1 2025, 7 min, not reviewed, 2,750 views). Give it category checkboxes (checking two shows both categories' posts), a reviewed-only toggle, and a box where I type a maximum read time — the three should narrow things down together, with a 'Showing X of 8 articles' line where X is however many match the current filters, split five per page, and if I filter while on page 2 just snap me back to page 1. Default order is most views first, and whenever two articles tie put the newer one on top. Two things I want everywhere in this app from now on, including anything we build later: read times always written like '9 min read', and every article showing either a 'Medically Reviewed' tag (with the doctor's name where there's room) or an 'Editorial' tag if nobody's reviewed it yet.
follow_ups.source_feature: Paginated article archive with result counts

ui_instruct.task: On the archive page, check the Nutrition category and switch on the reviewed-only toggle.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly two articles remain — Understanding Gut Bacteria and Beginner's Guide to Meal Prep — and the counter reads 'Showing 2 of 8 articles'.

ui_instruct.task: Open the archive page with no filters applied and look at the top of the list.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Sleep Debt: Myth or Real? sits above Understanding Gut Bacteria — both have 3,200 views, and the newer article wins the tie.

ui_instruct.task: On the archive page, type 5 into the maximum read time box.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Only the three articles of 5 minutes or less remain visible — Hydration Myths Debunked at exactly '5 min read', 10-Minute Morning Stretch Routine, and The Science of Cold Showers.

ui_instruct.task: From the archive, click the row for Understanding Gut Bacteria.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Its full article page opens and shows the Medically Reviewed tag naming Dr. Sam Wexler.

ui_instruct.task: Open any article and submit a comment that says 'Great tips, thanks!'.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The comment appears in the article's comment section immediately after posting.

follow_ups.instruction: Let's add one of those 'What's your wellness focus?' quizzes — five questions, four answer options each, every option clearly tagged with the topic it leans toward (Nutrition, Fitness, Sleep, or Mind), and picking an answer should hop straight to the next question. While I'm taking it I want to see where I stand: which question I'm on plus a running tally of my picks per topic, with a back button so changing an earlier answer redoes the tally instead of double-counting. At the end my focus is whichever topic I picked most — and if two topics tie, go with the one I picked more recently. The results card should then recommend that topic's articles from the archive, most-viewed first.

ui_instruct.task: Take the quiz, picking the Nutrition-tagged option on questions 1 and 3, the Fitness-tagged option on questions 2 and 4, and the Sleep-tagged option on question 5.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The results card names Fitness as the wellness focus — the two-two tie with Nutrition breaks toward Fitness because it was picked more recently.

ui_instruct.task: Start the quiz and answer question 1 with a Fitness-tagged option, then pause.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The running tally shows Fitness at 1 with the other topics at 0, and the progress indicator shows you are now on question 2 of 5 — all before the quiz is finished.

ui_instruct.task: Answer question 1 with a Fitness-tagged option, click the back control, and change your answer to a Sleep-tagged option.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The tally now shows Sleep at 1 and Fitness back at 0 — the old pick is removed, not double-counted.

ui_instruct.task: Finish the quiz picking a Fitness-tagged option every time, then look at the recommended articles on the results card.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The recommendations are Fitness articles listed most-viewed first — Strength Training After 50 on top — and each one shows an 'X min read' label plus its Medically Reviewed or Editorial tag.

ui_instruct.task: On the archive page, type 5 into the maximum read time box.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Only the three articles of 5 minutes or less remain visible — Hydration Myths Debunked at exactly '5 min read', 10-Minute Morning Stretch Routine, and The Science of Cold Showers.

follow_ups.instruction: Time for a community area: give each of our four topics its own discussion board, with a link to each board right on that topic's category page. Seed Nutrition with 'Best protein sources for vegetarians?' from May 2, 2025 carrying 4 replies and 'Is intermittent fasting safe?' from Apr 11, 2025 also carrying 4 replies, Fitness with 'Knee pain after running' from Mar 22, 2025 with 1 reply, Sleep with 'Can't fall asleep before 2am' from May 9, 2025 with no replies yet, and leave the Mind board empty for now. Anyone can start a thread with a title and body, open one to reply, and the community landing page should roll up each board's thread and reply totals; inside a board, each thread is listed with its reply count, and the busiest threads go first (most replies, and the newer one wins a tie). Also — and this goes for any list anywhere in this app, now and for whatever we add later — if there's nothing in it, show a friendly nudge to get things started instead of a blank space.

ui_instruct.task: Open the Nutrition discussion board.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly two threads show, with 'Best protein sources for vegetarians?' listed above 'Is intermittent fasting safe?' — both have 4 replies, and the newer May 2 thread wins the tie.

ui_instruct.task: In the Fitness board, open 'Knee pain after running', type a reply saying 'Try foam rolling' and post it, then go back to the board's thread list.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The reply appears in the thread and the thread's reply count in the board list now shows 2.

ui_instruct.task: Open the Mind discussion board.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Instead of a blank area, a friendly message says there's nothing here yet and nudges you to start the first thread.

ui_instruct.task: Go to the Nutrition category page and click its link to the discussion board.
ui_instruct.expected_result: You land on the Nutrition board showing its two seeded threads.

ui_instruct.task: On the archive page, check the Nutrition category and switch on the reviewed-only toggle.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly two articles remain — Understanding Gut Bacteria and Beginner's Guide to Meal Prep — and the counter reads 'Showing 2 of 8 articles'.

follow_ups.instruction: Readers keep dropping health questions into article comments where they get lost — let's steer them to the community instead. Add an 'Ask the Community' helper: a box where someone types their question, and while they type — every keystroke, no submit button — it works out which of our four discussion boards the question belongs on. Give each topic a little keyword list (protein, meal, snack for Nutrition; workout, knee, muscle for Fitness; sleep, insomnia, nap for Sleep; stress, anxiety, focus for Mind — case shouldn't matter), count how many of a topic's words appear in the question, and route to the topic with the most hits; when two topics tie, the one whose keyword shows up earliest in the question takes it. Show the winning board along with the keywords that clinched it, list that board's existing threads right underneath so people can check whether someone's already asked, and add a post button that jumps to that board with a new thread already titled with their question, ready to submit.

ui_instruct.task: Type 'My knee hurts after every workout and my sleep is a mess' into the Ask the Community box.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The helper routes to the Fitness board — two keyword hits (knee, workout) beat Sleep's single hit even though 'sleep' comes last — and beneath the verdict it lists Fitness's one seeded thread, 'Knee pain after running'.

ui_instruct.task: Type 'Does stress ruin sleep?' into the Ask the Community box.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The helper routes to the Mind board — the one-hit tie between Mind (stress) and Sleep (sleep) breaks toward stress because it appears first in the question — and since the Mind board has no threads yet, the duplicate-check list shows a friendly nothing-here message with a nudge rather than a blank space.

ui_instruct.task: Slowly type 'How much protein do I need' into the Ask the Community box, watching after each keystroke.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The moment the word 'protein' is completed the helper flips to the Nutrition board and lists its two seeded threads — all without pressing Enter or clicking anything.

ui_instruct.task: Type 'Is a short nap good for sleep debt?' into the Ask the Community box, click the post button, and submit the pre-filled thread.
ui_instruct.expected_result: You land on the Sleep board with the new-thread form already titled 'Is a short nap good for sleep debt?', and after submitting, the new thread sits at the top of the board above 'Can't fall asleep before 2am' — both are replyless, so the newer thread wins.

ui_instruct.task: Take the quiz, picking the Nutrition-tagged option on questions 1 and 3, the Fitness-tagged option on questions 2 and 4, and the Sleep-tagged option on question 5.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The results card names Fitness as the wellness focus — the two-two tie with Nutrition breaks toward Fitness because it was picked more recently.

follow_ups.instruction: Our credibility push: build a Review Desk where everything still tagged Editorial sits in a queue waiting for a medical once-over. Opening a queued article shows its text plus a two-item checklist — sources verified, claims accurate — and a place to pick the reviewer (Dr. Lena Ortiz or Dr. Sam Wexler); approving stays off until both boxes are ticked and a reviewer's chosen, and there's also a request-changes option with a note that keeps it Editorial but flags it in the queue. The moment something's approved it should leave the queue and flip to Medically Reviewed with the doctor's name everywhere — its article page, the archive, the reviewed-only filter, all of it. Set up 'Managing Stress at Work' with both boxes already ticked and Dr. Sam Wexler picked, so I can demo a one-click approval.
follow_ups.source_feature: Medical review / fact-check badge on articles

ui_instruct.task: Open the Review Desk.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The queue holds exactly four articles — Sleep Debt: Myth or Real?, Managing Stress at Work, Hydration Myths Debunked, and The Science of Cold Showers — only the Editorial ones, not all eight.

ui_instruct.task: At the Review Desk, open Sleep Debt: Myth or Real?, tick both checklist items but leave the reviewer unpicked, and try to approve.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Approval is blocked (button disabled or a clear message) until a reviewer is chosen; the article stays in the queue tagged Editorial.

ui_instruct.task: At the Review Desk, open Managing Stress at Work and click approve, then return to the queue.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The queue now holds three articles with Managing Stress at Work gone, and its article page now shows Medically Reviewed with Dr. Sam Wexler.

ui_instruct.task: At the Review Desk, open Managing Stress at Work and click approve, then go to the archive and switch on the reviewed-only toggle.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Five articles now pass the reviewed-only filter, and Managing Stress at Work is among them.

ui_instruct.task: Open the archive page with no filters applied and look at the top of the list.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Sleep Debt: Myth or Real? sits above Understanding Gut Bacteria — both have 3,200 views, and the newer article wins the tie.

follow_ups.instruction: Newsletter time — build me a 'This Week in Health' digest composer. It should only offer Medically Reviewed articles to pick from (anything Editorial has to clear the Review Desk before it can show up here) and cap a digest at five picks, and while I'm choosing I want a live summary of how many I've added plus the combined read time, updating with every add or remove. Generating the digest produces an on-screen text preview I can copy, grouped by topic with each article's read time. There's also a subscribe box for readers — only accept an email with an @ and a dot somewhere after it, showing a clear inline error otherwise and a confirmation when it's good.
follow_ups.source_feature: Newsletter / email subscription with a free report incentive

ui_instruct.task: Open the digest composer and add every article it offers.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly four articles are offered — Understanding Gut Bacteria, Beginner's Guide to Meal Prep, 10-Minute Morning Stretch Routine, and Strength Training After 50 — and with all four added the live summary reads 4 picks totaling '33 min read'.

ui_instruct.task: In the digest composer, add Understanding Gut Bacteria and 10-Minute Morning Stretch Routine, then remove Understanding Gut Bacteria.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The live summary first shows '13 min read' for the two picks, then drops to 1 pick at '4 min read' after the removal — no stale total.

ui_instruct.task: In the digest subscribe box, type sam@wellness and submit, then change it to sam@wellness.com and submit again.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The first attempt shows an inline error and no confirmation; the second shows a success confirmation.

ui_instruct.task: At the Review Desk, open Managing Stress at Work and click approve, then open the digest composer.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The composer now offers five articles, with Managing Stress at Work newly available to pick.

ui_instruct.task: In the Fitness board, open 'Knee pain after running', type a reply saying 'Try foam rolling' and post it, then go back to the board's thread list.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The reply appears in the thread and the thread's reply count in the board list now shows 2.

follow_ups.instruction: I want an engagement dashboard so we can see what's actually landing. Score every article as views divided by read-time minutes, shown to one decimal (Meal Prep should read 120.8, not 121), with a top-three 'Trending This Week' leaderboard by that score — I know Gut Bacteria has huge raw views, but per minute it shouldn't beat Managing Stress at Work. Add per-topic rollups too: total article views for each topic sitting next to that topic's board activity (threads and replies) so we can spot where people talk versus read. And give me a box where I type a score cutoff and it highlights every article at or above it, with a small count of how many made the cut.

ui_instruct.task: Open the engagement dashboard and read the Trending This Week leaderboard.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The top three are Sleep Debt: Myth or Real? (533.3), Managing Stress at Work (392.9), then Understanding Gut Bacteria (355.6) — score order, not raw-view order.

ui_instruct.task: On the engagement dashboard, type 245 into the score cutoff box.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly four articles are highlighted, including 10-Minute Morning Stretch Routine sitting right at 245.0, and the count of matches reads 4.

ui_instruct.task: On the engagement dashboard, find the Nutrition rollup.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Nutrition shows 5,260 total article views alongside its board activity of 2 threads and 8 replies.

ui_instruct.task: In the Fitness board, open 'Knee pain after running', post a reply saying 'Same here', then open the engagement dashboard and check the Fitness rollup.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The Fitness board activity now counts 2 replies, reflecting the reply you just posted.

ui_instruct.task: At the Review Desk, open Sleep Debt: Myth or Real?, tick both checklist items but leave the reviewer unpicked, and try to approve.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Approval is blocked (button disabled or a clear message) until a reviewer is chosen; the article stays in the queue tagged Editorial.

follow_ups.instruction: The look needs a refresh — keep the misty rose background, but: every primary action button (post comment, start thread, quiz answers' submit and the like, subscribe) goes deep teal with white text; every page's main heading gets centered; article and thread cards get 12px rounded corners with a soft drop shadow; the Medically Reviewed tag becomes a green pill and Editorial a gray pill; and all dates render in italics. Apply it everywhere — homepage, the archive, the community pages, the quiz — no page left half on the old style.
follow_ups.source_feature: Medical review / fact-check badge on articles

ui_instruct.task: Open any article page and look at its comment submit button, then open a community board and look at the start-a-thread control.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Both are deep teal with white text — the same primary-action styling on both pages.

ui_instruct.task: Open the archive and look at the cards for Understanding Gut Bacteria and Sleep Debt: Myth or Real?.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Understanding Gut Bacteria carries a green Medically Reviewed pill and Sleep Debt: Myth or Real? a gray Editorial pill, both on rounded cards with a soft shadow.

ui_instruct.task: Visit the homepage, the archive, and the community landing page and look at each page's main heading and any visible dates.
ui_instruct.expected_result: All three headings are centered and the dates shown on those pages are in italics.

ui_instruct.task: Finish the wellness quiz picking any option on each question and look at the results card.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The recommended articles on the card use the new green/gray pill badges, and any action button on the card is deep teal with white text.

ui_instruct.task: In the digest subscribe box, type sam@wellness and submit, then change it to sam@wellness.com and submit again.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The first attempt shows an inline error and no confirmation; the second shows a success confirmation.

follow_ups.instruction: Last big one: a My Feed page that's actually mine. It blends two sources — the topics I follow and whatever focus my latest quiz run landed on — into one article list, but keep it snackable: only each source topic's top two most-viewed articles make the cut (the newer one wins a view tie), and the survivors merge into a single list ordered most-viewed first with that same tie-break. When a topic comes from both sources its articles still appear exactly once, tagged with where they came from ('Following', 'Quiz pick', or both). Let me toggle my followed topics on and off right on the feed, and start me out already following Nutrition and Sleep.

ui_instruct.task: Open the My Feed page fresh, before taking any quiz.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly three articles show, in this order: Sleep Debt: Myth or Real? first, Understanding Gut Bacteria second (the 3,200-view tie breaks to the newer one), then Beginner's Guide to Meal Prep — Hydration Myths Debunked stays out because only Nutrition's top two make the feed.

ui_instruct.task: On the My Feed page, toggle the Sleep topic off.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Sleep Debt: Myth or Real? disappears, leaving just Nutrition's top two — Understanding Gut Bacteria and Beginner's Guide to Meal Prep — each still tagged as coming from a followed topic.

ui_instruct.task: On the My Feed page, toggle both Nutrition and Sleep off without having taken the quiz.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The feed shows a friendly nothing-here message with a nudge to act — not a blank area or a crash.

ui_instruct.task: Take the wellness quiz picking a Nutrition-tagged option on every question, then open My Feed.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The feed still shows exactly three articles — no duplicates even though Nutrition is both followed and the quiz focus — and the two Nutrition articles now carry both the Following and Quiz-pick tags.

ui_instruct.task: Type 'My knee hurts after every workout and my sleep is a mess' into the Ask the Community box.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The helper routes to the Fitness board — two keyword hits (knee, workout) beat Sleep's single hit even though 'sleep' comes last — and beneath the verdict it lists Fitness's one seeded thread, 'Knee pain after running'.

target_app_summary: The little health blog has grown into a full wellness publishing platform. Discovery grew two ways: a filterable, paginated article archive with review-status and read-time screening, and a personalized My Feed that reconciles followed topics with quiz results into a top-two-per-topic list with provenance tags. Engagement grew into per-topic community boards with a reply workflow, a live question router that classifies a typed question onto the right board keystroke-by-keystroke and posts it as a pre-titled thread, and an engagement analytics dashboard that scores articles by views-per-minute and rolls up board activity. An editorial pipeline (Review Desk) gates which articles earn the Medically Reviewed badge, which in turn gates what the weekly digest composer may include — a three-deep chain from the seeded archive through review to the digest. A site-wide visual refresh (teal actions, badge pills, centered headings) ties the surfaces together, and app-wide conventions (min-read formatting, Reviewed/Editorial labels, friendly empty states) are enforced silently on every new surface.

edges.what: base blog articles and article pages the archive lists and links to
archive articles ranked by view counts for result-card recommendations
topic categories and category pages that host board links
routed questions land on the seeded boards; the winning board's threads are listed for duplicate checks and the pre-titled question posts there as a new thread
badge flip rendered on base article pages
approval moves articles into the archive's reviewed-only filter
Review Desk approval gates digest eligibility
read-time metadata summed into the live digest total
views and read times feed the views-per-minute score
board thread/reply activity aggregated per topic
restyles archive cards and badge pills
restyles quiz flow and results card
restyles the digest subscribe button as a teal primary action
followed topics drive the feed's contents
latest quiz focus adds its topic's articles to the feed
feed items ranked by archive view counts with badge/read-time labels

global_rules.rule: Every article, anywhere it appears (lists, search results, quiz recommendations, digest, feed), carries either a 'Medically Reviewed' tag (with the doctor's name where there's room) or an 'Editorial' tag.
Read times are always written as 'X min read' everywhere in the app.
Any empty list or section anywhere shows a friendly nothing-here message with a nudge to act, never a blank area.
